title: Tame trait quotient and change of logarithmic base
statement:
A trait is $\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. It is complete strictly henselian if $R$ is complete for that ideal, is henselian (simple roots of monic polynomials over its residue field lift), and has separably closed residue field. Its canonical log structure is $\mathcal O\cap j_*\mathcal O_\eta^\times$, where $j$ includes its generic point. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic.

Let $S^{\prime}\to S$ be a finite dominant extension of complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic traits. Let a finite group $H$ act on $S^{\prime}$ over $S$, with $\#H$ invertible on $S$. Put $R^{\prime}=\Gamma(S^{\prime},\mathcal O_{S^{\prime}})$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}((R^{\prime})^H)$, where $(R^{\prime})^H=\{r:h(r)=r\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. Then $T$ is a complete strictly henselian trait, $T\to S$ is finite dominant, and $S^{\prime}\to T$ is finite dominant and log etale for the canonical fs log structures [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale, def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Its generic-field degree divides $\#H$, allowing a nonfaithful action. For every locally Noetherian fs log scheme $V$ log smooth over $S^{\prime}$, the composite $V\to T$ is log smooth. Here finite means affine with module-finite coordinate algebras [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and dominant means having dense image.

source.place: Expose XVI 3.7, p.254, sentences from T=S prime/H through log smoothness over T; Expose VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72, for tame Kummer charts.
